incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @maria_oncall: p99 latency breach detected for customer TempoHealth on streaming endpoints (p95 420ms, p99 6.8s) -- runbook /runbooks/streaming-tail.md || @channel

maria_oncall: seeing the alert, joining. any idea if this is single-tenant or cross-tenant?

leo: traffic spike is concentrated to TempoHealth (single-tenant). their session concurrency jumped ~3x over last 5m.

maria_oncall: is this the usual long-prefix issue?

tempohealth-sre: hi all, we pushed a client change about 10m ago that bundles multiple user prompts into a single request for prefetching. that might explain it.

sanjay: that could cause strange tokenization/kv-cache churn if each bundle has unrelated prefixes. p99s go up when KV cache misses and we re-warm repeatedly.

leo: confirming logs: many sessions show repeated cache invalidations and a burst of hot keys. stack shows streaming stalls waiting on KV read. snippet: ```
[2026-03-10T12:14:21Z] session=th-xyz cache_miss=true kv_reads=324 pending_streams=11
```

maria_oncall: ok immediate mitigations: 1) throttle tempohealth concurrency at edge, 2) route them to dedicated pool with larger per-session cache, 3) enable temporary prefix-merge to avoid repeated cache churn. i'm going to run the throttle now.

maria_oncall: `redwoodctl traffic throttle --customer tempohealth --concurrency 30 --reason "emergency p99 mitigation"`

ops-bot: Command queued: throttle policy applied to customer tempohealth (concurrency=30).

leo: applying route to dedicated-03 with higher cache. `redwoodctl route set --customer tempohealth --pool dedicated-03 --sticky true`

ops-bot: Route change accepted; draining existing sessions into dedicated-03 (expected window ~45s).

tempohealth-sre: thanks — rolling back the client bundling change now and will patch to stop bundling unrelated prompts.

sanjay: I'm also dropping their request burst into a separate QoS lane so non-TempoHealth traffic doesn't degrade.

maria_oncall: monitoring dashboards: p95/p99 panels reloaded. current numbers: p95 260ms (down from 420), p99 1.6s (down from 6.8s) — still above internal SLO for streaming p99 1.0s but improving.

leo: note: we saw a couple of streaming stalls tied to a kernel selection fallback when sequence length estimation overshot. i've opened infra issue #INC-563 to force a safer kernel selection for dedicated-03.

maria_oncall: handoff plan: if p99 < 1.2s in 10m, we'll keep throttles and route until TempoHealth deploys the client fix. if p99 > 1.5s re-escalate page infra and open a pagerduty incident. assigning to @sanjay for next shift.

maria_oncall: @sanjay you're on-call for follow-up at 12:45Z. checklist for handoff: 
- confirm TempoHealth deploy rollback completed
- monitor KV cache hit-rate at session granularity
- keep throttle in place until client patch in prod
- coordinate with infra to apply kernel selection patch if stalls return

sanjay: received, will take over at 12:45Z. linking the runbook and relevant logs: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/streaming-tail.md 

tempohealth-sre: we rolled back the bundling. will confirm after a few minutes of normal traffic. apologies for the interruption.

maria_oncall: thanks. leaving this thread open for the handoff and will close when p99 consistently below 1.0s and client fix in prod. :white_check_mark:
